settings.title: Settings
settings.list.browser: A machine's own settings are on the desktop, where the machine is.
settings.theme.label: Theme
settings.theme.hint: System follows the computer's own light or dark setting.
settings.language.label: Language
settings.language.hint: The window's own words, and Daoris's lines on a session's record. What agents, people and the service write is shown as written.
settings.plugins.title: Installed plugins
settings.plugins.why: What each plugin installed here holds set: whether it is on, and each server's approval for Ask Daoris with the writes accepted. A plugin's settings are changed on its own page; Open leads there.
settings.plugins.holdsNone: Holds nothing set but whether it is on.
settings.plugins.server.changed: changed since you approved it: asks again
settings.notify.body: Nobody should have to watch a driver. This machine can tell you as it happens: a session stops to ask you something, holds a tool call for your answer, answers your words, or ends without you asking; a quest parks on its failed sessions; a start waits for an account. Never for an ending you caused, because a notice about what you just pressed is one you learn to dismiss unread.
settings.notify.label: Announce what needs you or ended
settings.notify.terminal: Also `daoris settings notify on|off` — one file, either door; a machine with no screen says it on its console.
settings.notify.state.on: On: a park, a held tool call, an answer to your words and an ending you did not ask for are each said, in the window you are at or by a system notification while Daoris is behind.
settings.notify.state.off: Off: none of these is said, and Notifications still lists each one.
settings.notify.press: A terminal's press for your confirmation is said either way: its terminal waits on your answer.
settings.uxTrail.label: Keep a UX trail
settings.uxTrail.body: This window keeps the pages you open and the buttons you press, and how long a step waiting on you took to be pressed, on this desktop only. Never what you type or a field's value. Off by default.
settings.uxTrail.state.on: On: kept under the home's ux-trail folder, one file a day.
settings.notify.on: This machine will announce what needs you or ended.
settings.notify.off: This machine will announce only a terminal's press for your confirmation. Notifications still lists everything.
settings.cap.label: Sessions at once on this machine
settings.cap.terminal: Also `daoris settings cap <n>` — one file, either door.
settings.cap.body: How many sessions Daoris starts at once on this machine, across every repository. It counts the sessions Daoris starts, never a conversation you hold yourself. Raise it when too few sessions are working; lower it to spend less at a time.
settings.cap.set: Daoris now starts at most {{count}} session at once on this machine.
settings.cap.set_other: Daoris now starts at most {{count}} sessions at once on this machine.
settings.cooloff.label: Cool-off when no time is named
settings.cooloff.terminal: Also `daoris settings cooloff <minutes>` — one file, either door.
settings.cooloff.body: When an agent refuses a turn for its account's limit and names no time it resets, the account cools this many minutes before Daoris starts on it again. Long enough that a spent account is not started on at every look; short enough that a wrong guess costs an hour, not an evening. A limit that names its reset cools until then.
settings.cooloff.set: An account whose agent names no reset now cools {{count}} minute.
settings.cooloff.set_other: An account whose agent names no reset now cools {{count}} minutes.
settings.quiet.label: Look in on a quiet session after
settings.quiet.terminal: Also `daoris settings quiet <minutes>`, from 5 to 120 — one file, either door.
settings.quiet.body: A session is never stopped for running long. One that says nothing and runs nothing for this long gets Daoris's help: a word, then your choice or a fresh start of the same work.
settings.quiet.set: Daoris now looks in on a session quiet for {{count}} minute.
settings.quiet.set_other: Daoris now looks in on a session quiet for {{count}} minutes.
settings.drain.label: An update holds new work for at most
settings.drain.terminal: Also `daoris settings drain <minutes>`, from 1 to 120 — one file, either door.
settings.drain.body: A staged build installs when the work running ends, and nothing new starts meanwhile. Past this bound new work starts again, and the build installs at the first moment nothing runs.
settings.drain.set: An update now holds new work for {{count}} minute at most.
settings.drain.set_other: An update now holds new work for {{count}} minutes at most.
settings.vacancy.label: A vacant step is given up after
settings.vacancy.terminal: Also `daoris settings vacancy <hours>`, from 1 to 720 — one file, either door.
settings.vacancy.body: A step that waits on a role its agent holds, when no agent's session answers it, is listed under Vacant. Past this bound Daoris stops it as its own, with what it tried, and its run ends as gave up; it is never asked of you.
settings.vacancy.set: A vacant step is now given up after {{count}} hour.
settings.vacancy.set_other: A vacant step is now given up after {{count}} hours.
settings.reserve.label: Kept free for your own work
settings.reserve.terminal: Also `daoris settings reserve <gb>|auto`, a number of GB from 0 to 1024 — one file, either door.
settings.reserve.body: You run your own work on this machine too. Daoris keeps free the larger of this floor and what your own work is measured to take back (how far its use has stood above its present in the last ten minutes, and a margin). A heavy run, a check or a build starts only while the free memory stays at or above that after its own need, learned from its own earlier runs here; a new one waits while it is under, and its wait says why. 0 or auto sets no floor.
settings.reserve.auto: Measured from your own work (no floor)
settings.reserve.state: Keeping {{kept}} GB free. This machine: {{total}} GB of memory, {{free}} GB free commit; Daoris's own processes hold {{daoris}} GB.
settings.reserve.stateNone: Keeping nothing back. This machine: {{total}} GB of memory, {{free}} GB free commit; Daoris's own processes hold {{daoris}} GB.
settings.reserve.set: The machine now keeps at least {{gb}} GB free for your own work.
settings.reserve.setNone: The machine now has no floor for your own work: only what it is measured to take back stays free.
settings.reserve.setAuto: The machine now keeps free what your own work is measured to take back, with no floor.
settings.reserve.why: Why: your own work holds {{person}} GB and has stood {{swing}} GB higher in the last ten minutes, plus a {{margin}} GB margin; the {{by}} sets what is kept.
settings.reserve.room: Room: {{limit}} of {{ceiling}} heavy runs at once ({{signal}}{{busy}}); a gate needs {{need}} GB ({{source}}).
settings.reserve.signal.memory: backed off: free memory under what is kept
settings.reserve.signal.timeouts: backed off: a run's tests timed out under load
settings.reserve.source.learned: learned from {{runs}} runs on this machine
settings.reserve.source.declared: declared, until it has run here
settings.terminal.label: A terminal's presses
settings.terminal.terminal: Also `daoris settings terminal ask|act` — one file, either door; set from a terminal, it asks you here first.
settings.terminal.body: Any program on this machine can send Daoris a press as yours, so by default each one waits for your Confirm in this window. Turn this on while an agent you run yourself, outside Daoris, works on Daoris from its terminal: each press it sends then runs at once as yours and is listed in Notifications. A session Daoris started keeps its own access, and a program inside one of Daoris's agents still asks.
settings.terminal.state.ask: Ask: each press from a terminal on this machine waits for your Confirm here.
settings.terminal.state.act: Act: a press from a terminal on this machine that no Daoris session owns runs at once as yours, listed in Notifications.
settings.terminal.set.ask: A press from a terminal now waits for your Confirm.
settings.terminal.set.act: A press from a terminal now runs at once as yours.
settings.manifest.label: A folder is too large to follow past
settings.manifest.terminal: Also `daoris settings manifest files <n>` and `minutes <n>`, from 1,000 files and 1 to 60 minutes — one file, either door.
settings.manifest.body: Before a session works in a folder, Daoris lists its files so it can say what changed meanwhile. A folder with more files than this, or one whose listing takes longer than this, is too large to follow: it still works in place, one session at a time, but its session is told nothing of what changed meanwhile and its changes are not listed. Raise either if a large folder should be followed; lower them to spend less time at each start.
settings.manifest.files: Most files a folder's manifest lists
settings.manifest.minutes: Most minutes a folder's manifest read takes
settings.manifest.setFiles: Daoris now follows a folder of up to {{count}} file.
settings.manifest.setFiles_other: Daoris now follows a folder of up to {{count}} files.
settings.manifest.setMinutes: Daoris now spends up to {{count}} minute listing a folder's files.
settings.manifest.setMinutes_other: Daoris now spends up to {{count}} minutes listing a folder's files.
settings.manifest.copyLabel: A folder is copied for a session working apart up to
settings.manifest.copyTerminal: Also `daoris settings manifest copy <megabytes>`, from 1 MB — the same file, either door.
settings.manifest.copyBody: A department whose workflow sets its sessions apart gives each a copy of its folder, brought back file by file after your review. A folder past this size, past 20,000 files, or with less than twice its size free on the disk is not copied: its session waits and says how to go on, and never works in your folder in the copy's place. Raise it to copy larger folders.
settings.manifest.copy: Most megabytes a folder may hold to be copied
settings.manifest.setCopy: Daoris now copies a folder of up to {{count}} MB for a session working apart.
settings.manifest.setCopy_other: Daoris now copies a folder of up to {{count}} MB for a session working apart.
